questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #66: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Hit the nail on the head'
options: To state something with exact accuracy
questions.hint: To describe exactly what is causing a situation.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #67: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Beat around the bush'
options: To avoid discussing the main topic directly
questions.hint: To speak evasively without coming to the point.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #68: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Call it a day'
options: To stop working on something for the rest of the day
questions.hint: To decide to stop working.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #69: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Once in a blue moon'
questions.hint: An event that happens very rarely.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #70: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Through thick and thin'
options: Under all circumstances, good and bad
questions.hint: Supporting someone through all difficulties.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #71: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To spill the beans'
questions.hint: 'Spill the beans' means to reveal secret information.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #72: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Bite the bullet'
options: To face a difficult situation with courage
To get injured in a fight
questions.hint: 'Bite the bullet' means to endure a painful situation bravely.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #73: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'A blessing in disguise'
options: An apparent misfortune that yields unexpected good results
questions.hint: Something that seems bad at first but turns out good.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #74: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Burn the midnight oil'
options: To work or study late into the night
questions.hint: To study or work until late at night.

questions.question: English Idioms & Phrases #75: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Throw in the towel'
questions.hint: To give up or accept defeat.

questions.question: English Grammar & Usage #1: Neither of the two candidates (A) / have submitted (B) / their original documents (C) / on time (D).
questions.hint: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb.

questions.question: English Grammar & Usage #2: The scenery of Kashmir (A) / are very (B) / charming and (C) / picturesque (D).
questions.hint: 'Scenery' is an uncountable singular noun.

questions.question: English Grammar & Usage #3: No sooner did he arrive ______ the meeting started.
questions.hint: 'No sooner did...' is followed correlatively by 'than'.

questions.question: English Grammar & Usage #4: The candidate was accused ______ tampering with evidence.
questions.hint: 'Accused' takes the preposition 'of'.

questions.question: English Grammar & Usage #5: He has been living in Delhi ______ 2015.
questions.hint: 'Since' specifies a starting point in time.

questions.question: English Grammar & Usage #6: Convert to Passive Voice: 'The mechanic repaired the damaged engine.'
options: The mechanic was repairing the engine.
The engine is repaired by mechanic.
The damaged engine was repaired by the mechanic.
The engine has been repaired by mechanic.
questions.hint: Past simple 'repaired' converts to 'was repaired'.

questions.question: English Grammar & Usage #7: Choose the correct indirect speech: 'He said, "I am learning English."'
options: He told he is learning English.
He said that he was learning English.
He said that he had learned English.
He said that I was learning English.
questions.hint: Present continuous 'am learning' shifts to past continuous 'was learning'.

questions.question: English Grammar & Usage #8: Convert to Active Voice: 'A song was being sung by Lata.'
questions.hint: 'was being sung' converts to active 'was singing'.
